bill.title: A resolution designating February 16, 2026, as "National Elizabeth Peratrovich Day".
bill.latestActionText: Submitted in the Senate, considered, and agreed to without amendment and with a preamble by Unanimous Consent. (consideration: CR S716; text: CR S711)
bill.officialSummary: This resolution designates February 16, 2026, as National Elizabeth Peratrovich Day. It also encourages the people of the United States and Members of Congress to commemorate the life and civil rights advocacy of Elizabeth Wanamaker Peratrovich by continuing the important work of ensuring equality for Alaska Natives and Native Americans.

classification.plainSummary:
This resolution designates February 16, 2026, as National Elizabeth Peratrovich Day. It also encourages the people of the United States and Members of Congress to commemorate the life and civil rights advocacy of Elizabeth Wanamaker Peratrovich by continuing the important work of ensuring equality for Alaska Natives and Native Americans.

This is a commemorative or honorific measure ("designating February 16, 2026, as "National Elizabeth Peratr"). It carries no sector tags and no donor overlap is computed for it, because attributing an economic interest to a commemorative or procedural measure would be misleading.

plain.whatItDoes: This is a tribute or a commemoration. It does not change any law.
plain.whoItTouches: Nobody directly — this is a statement, not a rule.
plain.everydayEffect: Nothing changes for you. No rule and no payment changes.
plain.source: From the bill title, and from the subject labels that library staff put on it.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
